Your requirement slug is: **axislabel-formatter-indexing**
Read /workspace/requirements/axislabel-formatter-indexing.yaml first — it is the authoritative statement of what must change.

This repo is a real snapshot of apache/echarts just before a set of real upstream commits. Your job is to work out, from the actual source code, exactly what the fix/feature must be, at the level of concrete code edits.

RULES:
- READ-ONLY on the repository. Do NOT modify, create, or delete ANY file under /workspace except the single plan file you are told to write below. Do NOT run any mutating git command (no add/commit/checkout/stash).
- Use Read/Grep/Glob/Bash(read-only) freely. Read the ACTUAL code — never guess at file contents or API shapes. Verify every symbol, option name, type name and file path you cite by opening the file.
- Search widely: src/, test/ut/spec/, test/*.html, index.d.ts, package.json, build/, theme/, ssr/, extension-src/. Related option types often live in src/component/**/[X]Model.ts, src/coord/**, src/util/types.ts, src/util/states.ts, src/label/*, src/scale/*.

1. **Goal** — restate what must change, in engineering terms.
2. **Findings** — the exact current code that is wrong/missing, with `path:line` references and quoted snippets of the current code.
3. **Plan** — an ordered list of edits. For EACH edit give: the file path, the exact anchor (existing code to search for, quoted verbatim so it can be matched), and the exact replacement/new code, fully written out and compilable TypeScript matching surrounding style (4-space indent, existing import conventions, Apache license header on new files).
4. **Tests** — whether a unit test under /workspace/test/ut/spec/... is feasible and, if so, sketch it (jest, ts-jest, uses `import { createChart } from '../core/utHelper'` style — CHECK an existing spec file for the real helper API before writing this).
5. **Verification** — what command(s) prove it works (e.g. `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs -t "..."`).
6. **Risks / open questions**.

Be exhaustive and concrete: another engineer must be able to apply your plan without re-deriving anything. If the requirement is vague, look for the smallest coherent real change that satisfies every acceptance signal in the yaml, and prefer touching the code paths the yaml names.

Finally return the structured summary object. `files` must list every repo file the plan will modify or create (excluding the plan file itself).

2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A chart author using custom axis label values needs labels to stay aligned with the same ordinal position they supplied, even when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent. Right now the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated values because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list instead of preserving the mapped position directly.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  When ECharts builds axis labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter should be called with the actual index of each rendered item in that filtered label sequence, including cases where the same numeric value appears more than once. Authors should be able to rely on formatter logic that branches on the index parameter without seeing duplicated values collapse onto the first matching position.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  For duplicate or repeated custom label values that remain in range, each rendered label keeps its own formatter index and produces the text a user would expect from its own slot in the sequence. Existing axis label rendering behavior, formatter signatures, and label text generation outside this indexing bug remain unchanged.
16	
17	  '

  `axisLabel.formatter` should receive the tick index as an additional argument so formatter logic can work reliably with `customValues`.

  A formatter declared as `axisLabel.formatter(value, index)` receives the expected index for each displayed custom tick and can build labels from that position information.

  '

  ## Acceptance signals

  A time axis that uses both `axisLabel.customValues` and `axisLabel.formatter` renders normally and passes the formatter the expected label values.

  '

Plan written to `/workspace/agent_plans/axislabel-formatter-indexing.md`. Repo is otherwise untouched (`git status` shows only the new `agent_plans/`).

Key findings:
- The bug is a single call site: `/workspace/src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:133-136`, in the `axisLabel.customValues` branch of `createAxisLabels()`. It does `zrUtil.map(ticks, numval => ... labelFormatter(tick) ...)` — the map index is discarded and the formatter gets **no** index argument.
- Everything downstream already supports the index: `makeLabelFormatter` is typed `(tick: ScaleTick, idx?: number) => string` (`/workspace/src/coord/axisHelper.ts:239`) and forwards `idx` to the user callback for non-category axes (`axisHelper.ts:274-287`); `makeRealNumberLabels` (same file, line 281-283) already uses the correct `map(ticks, (tick, idx) => labelFormatter(tick, idx))` pattern; `AxisLabelValueFormatter` already declares `index` (`axisCommonTypes.ts:239`).
- Verified empirically with a scratch jest run (test file kept outside the repo, in /tmp): `customValues: [-5, 1, 3, 3, 7, 20]` on a `value` axis with `min:0,max:10` produces tickValues `[1,3,3,7]` (filtering already correct) but formatter calls `[[1,undefined],[3,undefined],[3,undefined],[7,undefined]]`. A non-custom axis already gets `[[0,0],[2,1],…]`, so the fix must not touch that path.
- Fix: `zrUtil.map(ticks, (numval, index) => …, formattedLabel: labelFormatter(tick, index))` — the map index over the already-filtered `ticks` is exactly "index in the rendered label sequence" and gives duplicates distinct indices.
- Category axes are deliberately untouched: `makeLabelFormatter`'s category branch ignores `idx` and uses `tick.value - extent[0]` for back-compat (measured: `['a','c','a']` → `0,2,0`). The plan documents the exact optional edit in `axisHelper.ts` if the category case ever needs sequence indices, plus why it is safe w.r.t. `legacyContainLabel.ts:99`.
- Out of scope but flagged: time axis + `customValues` + function formatter currently throws at `/workspace/src/util/time.ts:346` — that is the separate `time-axis-customvalues-formatter` requirement (#21352); the new test avoids that combination.
- New test goes to `/workspace/test/ut/spec/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.test.ts` (already matched by `**/spec/coord/**/*.test.ts` in `test/ut/jest.config.cjs`); helper API (`createChart`, `getECModel`, `axis.getViewLabels()`, default-exported `CartesianAxisModel`) was confirmed by running an equivalent spec successfully.

input.summary: In `createAxisLabels()`'s `axisLabel.customValues` branch (src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts:133-136) the `zrUtil.map` iteration index is discarded and `labelFormatter(tick)` is called with no index, so user formatters on value/log/time axes receive `undefined` (and any value-based lookup would collapse repeated values onto the first match). The fix changes the callback to `(numval, index) => ... labelFormatter(tick, index)`, so each rendered label in the extent-filtered list keeps its own increasing index — verified by probe that `customValues: [-5,1,3,3,7,20]` on a 0..10 value axis yields ticks `[1,3,3,7]` and must produce indices `0,1,2,3`. A new spec test/ut/spec/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.test.ts asserts the custom-values indices and guards the unchanged non-custom path (`[[0,0],[2,1],…]`).
input.risk: Category axes are intentionally unchanged: makeLabelFormatter's category branch ignores the passed idx and uses `tick.value - extent[0]` for back-compat, so category customValues duplicates still report the ordinal offset (measured 0,2,0 for ['a','c','a']). If the hidden acceptance test asserts sequence indices for a category axis, the plan's documented optional edit in src/coord/axisHelper.ts (`idx != null ? idx : tick.value - extent[0]`) is needed. Time axis + customValues + function formatter still throws at src/util/time.ts:346 — that is the separate time-axis-customvalues-formatter (#21352) requirement and is deliberately not addressed; a textual overlap in that region is possible if both land. Time axes also see indices shifted by the first/last duplication in tickValuesToNumbers.
